title: The Common Man
dek: Pristinia’s tavern, where workers, musicians and adventurers met for meals, news, memorials and reunions.

facts.Function: Tavern, workplace, meeting and memorial space
facts.Fate: Green Beard sets the roof alight · 27–28 Jun 2026 quest postings (UTC)
facts.Successor: Pilgrim’s Hearth on the same foundations
facts.Owner: Herb Shepard · identified in the 14 Aug 2025 account
facts.Salvage: Basement stores and some tables and stools survive

body:
People kept returning to the Common Man. Adventurers drank there, civilians worked there, newcomers met the world there, musicians played for coppers, and memorials were held. As Pristinia grew, its shortages and need for labor became part of the tavern’s daily conversation.

Herb’s dwindling fruit and Farmer Frank’s exhaustion show a town feeding more mouths without enough farm labor. Lichen’s startling tip exposes the difference between adventurers’ wealth and Skye’s wages. Jiangshi later returns to the room where her memorial was held.

An ordinary room

The surviving record establishes wooden floors, tables, a bar and work area, food and drink service, and live music. The exact floor plan remains unrecovered. More important is the social mixture: farmers, tavern workers, chroniclers, adventurers, musicians, and visibly strange newcomers share the same room without an elite threshold.

The people who made it function

Herb wipes counters, remembers regulars’ orders, knows the stores, and turns local shortages into actionable civic knowledge. Serra serves patrons and notices how an adventurer’s absence changes tips. Alessio cleans mugs, works the tables, and makes the tavern legible as a workplace. Skye, a goblin bard, plays for coppers and connects newcomers to the First Forest and Al-Shomer traditions.

Ada, the town chronicler, drinks sweet ale while sketching a new face for an article. Pristinia’s public memory is therefore produced inside the same ordinary life it records. Farmer Frank brings the cost of failed harvest help into the room in his own exhaustion.

Hospitality, work and a place to begin

In the account posted on 16 March 2024, Nienna helps Gartina approach Herb about kitchen work. Gartina offers early-morning baking; Herb offers ingredients and modest pay, conditional on the goods selling, and Gartina accepts. This is one of the tavern’s practical connections between a newcomer’s skills and the town’s daily needs.

On 6 August, Herb explains that a stipend provides newcomers with a bunk and food while they get oriented. Later that month he credits paying Pristinia customers and a subsidy from Melian with keeping the cookfires lit and the liquor stocked. His beer, Tina’s Tincture, also remembers Gartina and her friends drying the fields so grain could be planted. Hospitality depends on work and reciprocal help, rather than an inexhaustible larder.

15 December 2024 · the town from below

Almost nothing epic happens. Herb cleans. Ada sketches. Skye plays. Frank rests after work. Alessio serves. Lichen enters. Aravil orders her usual tequila. Tobias orders ale. Sosdrielle dances. The tavern becomes unusually busy—and in doing so reveals how Pristinia actually lives.

Food, labor, and the next herd

Frank explains that adventurers promised harvest help but appeared only once while the settlement gained more mouths. Herb reports that sourdough remains available, dried fruit is running low, and Tina’s farm needs labor. He suggests hunting about a dozen elk while warning against damaging next year’s population. Immediate hunger does not erase stewardship of the future.

We was relyin’ on harvest help from these adventurers, with so many more mouths to feed and all. But damn, they only showed once.Farmer Frank

Aravil sees a possible role for herself as a hunter after hearing Herb describe the town’s need for meat. The opportunity comes from a civilian asking for help, without a formal proclamation.

Lichen and Skye

Lichen offers Skye ten gold pieces for music—roughly a year’s wages by Skye’s reaction. Skye refuses to exploit the mistake, accepts one coin, and begins telling Lichen about the First Forest. Adventurer-scale wealth and civilian-scale economy meet in the same room; restraint turns the collision into relationship.

A threshold into the world

The Common Man lets a person arrive without already holding a place in the world’s hierarchy. Enter town; enter the tavern; meet someone; hear a problem, history, or rumor; acquire a relationship; watch the world expand. By January 2026, Daffodil can flutter in, order tea, and meet Adelia and Jiangshi through the same soft threshold.

Memorial and return

The gathering posted on 25 May 2024 makes remembrance an organized act. Wren prepares food and drink and speaks for the fallen; Tricks plays softly, Dale contributes music, and Alyhotep gives a benediction. After the gathering, Wren helps clear the tankards but leaves the memorial in place. Private arguments run alongside the service, but the lasting civic act is the community making room for its dead.

Bitoshi first comes to Pristinia looking for Jiangshi and instead finds her memorial service at the Common Man. After Jiangshi returns, he later drinks beside her in the same room and remembers the memorial. The later event does not erase the earlier truth. The building holds both: she was mourned here, and she lived to return here.

On January 5, 2026, Jiangshi enters again to familiar scents and sounds. Adelia says only, “It’s been awhile.” Daffodil, Bitoshi, Oni, old relationships, newcomers, and talk of crops occupy one room. The tavern allows different eras of their lives to become simultaneous.

The fire

The quest record posted on 27–28 June 2026 (UTC) captures the fire itself. Green Beard throws a bead from his necklace onto the tavern, setting the roof alight. Herb escapes and calls the alarm. Gregory calls for a bucket line, and the townsfolk begin helping. Smoke fills the building before the narrator records the central ceiling collapsing and orders the adventurers out. These are source-posting dates, not an independently established world calendar.

In the following day’s cleanup, Nala Thilxed recalls an undead pirate crew whose captain wore a red-bead necklace. They had been asked to leave; she describes a confrontation with Rose, a fight inside and the captain escaping to fight outside. She says their group got out before the roof collapsed. Selwyn, who says he arrived near the end, also describes an escaped captain and later attributes the fire to a Fireball. These later survivor accounts have different vantage points. The recovered quest scene now independently establishes Green Beard’s arson and the collapse, while the full casualty count and the captain’s ultimate fate remain unresolved.

Herb and the people who returned

Herb is alive and clearing charred wood in the account posted on 29 June. He refuses to blame the adventurers, thanking them for doing what they could. Camilla Blackwood surveys the foundations and goes to check materials; Lady Severina brings ropes and water, with Øblivion available for hauling. Nala, Selwyn, Saelihn, Ibere, Karnak and Jangir appear among those helping. Karnak supplies wood and stone. These actions establish shared recovery work without assigning the entire rebuilding to one person.

Moving beams uncovers the charred but intact basement trapdoor. Herb opens it and finds the food and drinks safe. A few tables and stools can also be cleaned and repainted. He brings refreshments to the workers, insisting that they rest. The tavern’s service continues among the ruins before its replacement is finished.

Pilgrim’s Hearth

Posts dated 5 July describe a mostly finished tavern and its “new bones,” with debris still being cleared. Odo helps sweep despite having little personal history with the old place; Saelihn remembers helping bring cedar back to town. This records visible progress, not a definitive opening date. By 29 July, Pilgrim’s Hearth stands on the foundations as “a symbol of growth and change.” By September it is again an active social room for tea, news and ordinary conversation.

  1. Common Man

    Years of work, music, meals, memorial, newcomers, and returning patrons accumulate.

  2. Destruction

    Green Beard sets the roof alight in the quest scene posted 27–28 June 2026 (UTC); the narrator records its collapse.

  3. Same ground

    Pilgrim’s Hearth rises on the foundations rather than pretending the earlier place never existed.

  4. Ordinary life

    People again drink tea, exchange news, and carry old history without making every conversation about it.

The open record

The account posted on 14 August 2025 identifies Herb as the owner and barkeeper; his own introduction gives his name as Herb Shepard. A legal deed and the original founder remain unrecovered. Herb’s survival and salvaged stores and furniture are now established, but the fate of every staff member, the replacement’s complete building history and whether those furnishings were installed in the Hearth remain open. The fire itself now has a direct quest chronology.

Rescue followed by repair

After Farmer Frank’s family is rescued, Vigr and Cobble refuse repayment and offer to help restore his home. Cobble proposes hammer work and climbing; Vigr can haul and demolish. The celebration therefore ends with an offer of practical help, not a completed reconstruction.

Scene evidence: 1, 2, 3.

The room before the fire

The fire begins after a weekend in which the pirate crew has already made the Common Man unsafe. They eat without paying, curse, smash bottles and frighten the staff. Herb shelters beneath the bar and keeps serving drinks; the other bartenders stay away from the threatening room. The townspeople ask adventurers to remove the crew.

Outside, children look forward to seeing the pirates driven off while older onlookers hope it can happen peacefully. Herb tells Jéane Rose that he does not want a battle, but that the crew cannot stay. His request is to recover a workplace and public room already under occupation, before Green Beard turns the encounter into arson.

The narration identifies the smell of rotten flesh as coming from the pirates. Their captain’s later claims about who he once was remain his account. The fire and recovery account follows the confrontation and its consequences.

The bucket line and the order to get out

Herb escapes through the door and raises the alarm. At first the townspeople hesitate to come close while fighting continues inside. Gregory calls for a bucket line, and the narrator records people stepping forward to form it.

Smoke darkens the room and fills the adventurers’ lungs while the roof continues to hold. When the central ceiling finally collapses, the narrator orders everyone out immediately. The adventurers emerge injured and covered in ash. Outside, the townspeople keep the fire from spreading, although they cannot save the Common Man itself.

That limited success belongs beside the destruction: the building is lost, while the neighboring town is protected by people doing the work outside. The scene does not supply a complete list of staff casualties or confirm the captain’s ultimate fate.
